formulas.intro: Reference for how estimates, rate cards, variance, and KPIs are calculated. Client budget and delivery schedule can constrain AI extraction and are compared again after Calculate. Contact users (magic-link access) use the system rate card automatically. Full users use the selected rate card version when set; otherwise the active rate card. articles.title: Contact estimate access
articles.summary: Magic-link sign-in, one estimate per email, system rate card, and export limits.
articles.body: Visitors request access from the welcome page with email, name or company, and a Turnstile check. A magic link valid for 15 minutes signs them in and opens their estimate—one estimate per verified email. Contact users use the system rate card automatically (no rate card management UI). After calculation they may export up to three times per estimate in PDF, DOCX, Excel, or Markdown; each export is emailed to their address and PDFs include a Draft Estimate watermark. Administrators can upgrade contact accounts to full users with password login and rate card access.

articles.title: Quotation special notes
articles.summary: Admin-editable Special Notes for formal quotation PDF and DOCX exports.
articles.body: When a discount is applied, formal quotation exports (PDF quotation and DOCX quotation) include a Special Notes section. Administrators edit the Japanese and English title and body under Quotation settings. Placeholders {issue_date}, {special_price}, {original_price}, {discount_percent}, and {discount_amount} are replaced at export time. Detailed report exports are not affected.

articles.title: Rate card basics
articles.summary: How rate cards define roles, phases, and rates used in every estimate.
articles.body: Rate cards store hourly and daily rates by role, phase percentages, contingency, overhead, tax, setup costs, and monthly recurring items. The active rate card is applied when you calculate an estimate. Each user manages their own rate cards; administrators can access all cards. Cards used by existing estimates become locked—you can duplicate them to make changes without affecting past estimates.

articles.title: Export formats
articles.summary: Detailed report and formal quotation in PDF/DOCX, plus Excel and Markdown.
articles.body: After calculation, export from the estimate detail page. Choose detailed report or formal quotation for PDF and DOCX. Excel supports analysis; Markdown supports documentation. Display locale controls label language. Formal quotation exports include admin-configured Special Notes when a discount applies. faqs.question: What is AI Estimate?
faqs.answer: AI Estimate is an internal tool for creating software project estimates. Enter client and scope details in a structured project form, optionally upload requirement documents for AI extraction, and run a deterministic calculation engine to produce NRC, RC, and first-year cost totals in JPY.

faqs.question: Who can use the system?
faqs.answer: Two access paths exist. Contact users request a magic link from the welcome page—no password required—and receive one estimate per verified email with the system rate card. Full users sign in with email and password created by an administrator and can manage rate cards, multiple estimates, and the full feature set. Contact your administrator if you need a full account or cannot sign in.

faqs.question: What languages are supported?
faqs.answer: The interface is available in Japanese and English. Use the locale switcher in the header to change the UI language. After calculation, you can export estimates in either language.

faqs.question: What documents can I upload?
faqs.answer: Upload PDF and other supported document formats on an estimate. AI extracts a feature list with suggested effort hours. Always review and adjust AI suggestions before running the calculation.

faqs.question: What export formats are available?
faqs.answer: After calculation, export as a detailed report or formal quotation in PDF or DOCX, or as Excel and Markdown. Exports are available in Japanese or English. Formal quotation includes Special Notes when a discount is applied. Contact users may export up to three times per estimate; each export is emailed to their verified address and PDFs include a Draft Estimate watermark.

faqs.question: How does contact magic-link access work?
faqs.answer: From the welcome page, enter your email and complete the security check. You receive a one-time link valid for 15 minutes. Opening it signs you in and opens your estimate. Each verified email address may have one active contact estimate. Request a new link if the previous one expired.

faqs.question: Why is my export limit reached?
faqs.answer: Contact estimate access allows up to three exports per estimate (PDF, DOCX, Excel, or Markdown combined). Each successful export counts toward the limit and is emailed to your address. If you need additional exports, contact your administrator.

faqs.question: What do estimate statuses mean?
faqs.answer: Draft: form in progress. Extracting: AI is processing uploaded documents. Review: features ready for your edits. Calculated: costs have been computed. Exported: results have been exported at least once.

faqs.question: I cannot log in. What should I check?
faqs.answer: Verify your email and password. Disabled accounts cannot sign in. If problems persist, ask an administrator to confirm your account is active and reset your credentials if needed.

faqs.question: How does AI document extraction work?
faqs.answer: Upload PDF or other supported documents on an estimate. The system sends them for extraction and returns a feature list with suggested hours. Always review and adjust AI suggestions before calculating—the review step is required for accurate estimates.

documentation.title: NRC, RC, and first-year cost
documentation.summary: Overview of non-recurring, recurring, and combined first-year totals.
documentation.body: NRC (non-recurring cost) covers one-time effort: requirements through deployment, plus setup costs and applied contingency, overhead, and tax. RC (recurring cost) covers monthly items such as maintenance support multiplied over twelve months for the annual subtotal. First-year cost combines NRC with the annual RC total for a single-year project view.

documentation.title: Estimate workflow
documentation.summary: End-to-end flow from form entry to exported deliverable.
documentation.body: Contact users: request a magic link on the welcome page, verify email, and complete the project form on the auto-created estimate. Full users: create an estimate and complete the project form. Both paths: optionally upload documents for AI extraction, review and edit the feature list and hours, then run calculation (contact users use the system rate card automatically). Export in your preferred format when ready—contact users receive exports by email with a three-export limit and PDF watermark.

documentation.title: Rate card fields reference
documentation.summary: What each section of a rate card controls in calculations.
documentation.body: Roles define hourly and daily rates per team member type. Phases split effort across requirements, design, development, testing, and deployment—the percentages must sum to 100%. Contingency, overhead, and tax are applied as multipliers. Setup costs are one-time NRC line items. Monthly RC items add recurring charges. Development approach affects productivity assumptions used in effort calculations.
